title: Docs: add draft Optimize Guardrails overview + prompt set onboarding
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Draft public docs for Optimize Guardrails: overview, gating outcomes (pass/fail/timeout), and how to provide prompt sets for evaluation.
body: Summary: Adds the first draft of customer-facing documentation for Optimize Guardrails, focused on explaining what guardrails are, when/why gating runs, what users see in Console/API when gating passes/fails/times out, and how customers can supply prompt sets to improve coverage for their workloads. This is intentionally a draft (wording + final policy details will be refined during pilot), but it unblocks support enablement and gives design partners something concrete to react to. Motivation: Optimize can apply cost-saving config deltas (batching/caching/quantization/routing tweaks) that can impact output quality; we’re rolling out mandatory evaluation guardrails to prevent regressions. Customers have already asked (a) why an apply was blocked and (b) how to bring their own prompts/evals; this PR gives us a stable URL to point to during pilot. Scope (in docs only): (1) Product overview page explaining guardrails and the gating workflow, (2) “Gating results and statuses” section with definitions of pass/fail/timeout and what actions are available, (3) Prompt set onboarding guide (format, privacy notes, sampling guidance, and how prompt sets are versioned/revised), (4) API notes for the Optimize apply response shape (high level; actual schema is documented in API reference elsewhere), (5) FAQ and troubleshooting notes (common causes of failures and next steps). Explicitly out of scope: definitive threshold tables, model-family-specific exclusions, and any guarantee that specific metrics are used for every workload. Those details are in internal docs and may change during tuning; this draft describes the framework and where customers can inspect outcomes. Content notes: The wording avoids asserting that Redwood stores raw prompts long-term; instead it describes optional redaction, retention windows for artifacts, and that customers can choose what to provide. Also clarifies that guardrails are meant to prevent regressions, not prove “absolute quality.” Files/areas changed (high level): - docs/optimize/guardrails/index.mdx (new) - docs/optimize/guardrails/gating.mdx (new) - docs/optimize/guardrails/prompt-sets.mdx (new) - docs/optimize/guardrails/faq.mdx (new) - docs/optimize/guardrails/troubleshooting.mdx (new) - docs/optimize/_category_.json (updated nav) - docs/api/optimize/apply.mdx (small cross-link + note about gating) - src/components/Callout.tsx (minor style tweak for “Draft” callout) - src/content/partials/security-and-privacy.mdx (new shared partial for retention + PII guidance) Small illustrative snippet (from prompt-sets.mdx): “A prompt set is a versioned collection of representative inputs + expected evaluation criteria for a workload. Prompt sets can be uploaded as JSONL and tagged by route/workload (chat, tool-calling, structured output). During gating, Redwood runs the selected eval suite against the current config and the proposed config, then compares metrics under the configured thresholds.” Checklist: - [x] Add initial content pages - [x] Add nav entries and cross-links - [x] Add explicit ‘Draft during pilot’ disclaimer - [x] Include retention/PII guidance (non-authoritative; links to Security page) - [x] Add ‘What happens on timeout?’ guidance - [x] Run local build and link checker - [ ] Final legal/security wording for retention section (tracked in follow-up) - [ ] Add screenshots once UI states stabilize (tracked in follow-up) Follow-ups: - Add screenshots for Console gating panel once UX is finalized (Kenji / Console team). - Replace “high-level API notes” with links to generated OpenAPI fields once they land for gating output format. - Add a short “Design partner onboarding” section once pilot support process is finalized. Related work: ENG-3925 (Docs), PM-843 (gating UX states).
